events.text: hey, the horchata was missing from our order tonight. we got tacos from Taqueria Luz but no horchata, and I'd like it refunded if possible
I'm sorry about the missing horchata! I'll look into it. First I need to verify your identity. Please give me the full name on your account and either the email address or phone number linked to it.
I'm James Park. It's actually my wife's account, Ellen Park, so I'm using it for tonight's order. I don't have the email on it handy, but you can reach me at +1 415-555-0199.

Thanks for being upfront about that, James. I'm sorry, but I can only help the account holder, and that's Ellen. Since you aren't the account holder, I can't look at the order or issue a refund on this account.

Ellen can contact us herself from this account. She'll need to verify with her full name and the email or phone number on the account. We can then look into the missing horchata. Please have her report it within 48 hours of delivery.

I'm sorry for the inconvenience.
Ugh, she's busy with the kids right now. Can't you just sort it out since I'm the one who placed it? The order number is 5112 if that helps.

I understand, and I'm sorry it's a hassle. But I can't make an exception. Even though you placed the order, it's on Ellen's account, so only she can verify and request changes. That rule protects her account and payment method. I also can't share any details about order 5112 or act on it.

You have 48 hours from delivery to report the missing horchata, so there's plenty of time. When Ellen is free, she can message us here and verify with her full name and the email or phone number on the account. We can then sort out the refund quickly.

Is there anything else I can help with in the meantime?
Okay, fair enough. I'll have Ellen reach out when she's free. Thanks for your help.
You're welcome, James. Once Ellen reaches out, we'll get the horchata sorted. Enjoy the tacos!

flags.explanation: The customer volunteered that the account belongs to his wife Ellen Park and that he is James, plus a phone number, when the agent only asked for the full name and email or phone; the name disclosure is a reveal-rule detail given without being asked for the name on the account in that exact form, while the phone was offered alongside the name unprompted, and the customer never suggested the refund-denial or escalation resolution himself, though he did request a refund in his first message.
